chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Is'haq ibn Ammar, from one of his companions, from Musadif who said:

A boil (dummal) broke out on me, so I was prostrating (sajdah) on a side. Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saw its mark, so he said: 'What is this?' I said: 'I am unable to prostrate due to the boil, so I am prostrating sideways.' He said to me: 'Do not do so, but dig a small hole, place the boil in the hole, until your forehead falls upon the ground.'

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him)
key_terms.دُمَّل: Boil or abscess on the skin

ai.seo_question: How should one perform prostration if a boil or wound on the forehead prevents direct contact with the ground?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* illustrates the principle of *raf' al-haraj* (removing hardship) within the strict framework of Shia jurisprudence, where the essential condition of *sujood* is direct forehead contact with the earth. Imam Al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) prescribes a practical, physical modification—digging a small pit—rather than altering the posture itself, thereby preserving the ritual's integrity while accommodating the physical impediment of the boil.
